title: Holden Structured Intent
description: The only object the reasoning layer is allowed to emit toward the broker. Deliberately excludes: tier (derived server-side from `action` by the Policy Engine, never trusted from the caller), vendor (resolved by the broker from its own device inventory keyed on target.device_id, never asserted here), and any credential/secret material (the LLM never holds or transmits credentials).

intent_id.description: Unique per intent. Broker rejects replays of an already-seen intent_id.

correlation_id.description: Links this intent back to the diagnostic session/report that produced it, for audit trail reconstruction.

action.description: Abstract action name. Must match an entry in the broker's action catalog (broker/config/action-catalog.yaml). Not a CLI command or command fragment -- the Whitelist Compiler maps action+vendor to a fixed command template. An unrecognized action is rejected at the Intent Receiver before it reaches policy evaluation.

device_id.description: Broker looks this up in its own device inventory to resolve vendor/model/mgmt address. The intent never asserts vendor directly, so a compromised or hallucinating reasoning layer can't talk its way past a vendor-scoped whitelist by just claiming a device is something it isn't.

params.description: Action-specific parameters. Validated by the broker against the per-action param schema referenced in the action catalog entry for `action` -- not accepted as free-form input. Kept generic here because param shape varies per action; the envelope-level schema only guarantees this is a flat, JSON-serializable object (no nested executable content, no shell-like strings).

mode.description: propose: broker computes a dry-run diff only, no device contact (tier <=2, no approval required). execute: broker performs the actual device write (tier 3), and requires approval_token_ref to be present and to verify against the approval log for this exact intent_id.

approval_token_ref.description: Reference to a signed human-approval record (see rbac-role.schema.json approval block). Required when mode=execute and the resolved tier of `action` (looked up by the Policy Engine from the action catalog, not present in this envelope) is 3. Not enforceable as a static schema conditional here, precisely because tier is deliberately absent from this schema -- the Policy Engine rejects an execute-mode tier-3 intent missing this field at request time. This field is an authorization reference, not a credential -- the broker still mints its own short-lived device credential separately after verifying it.

justification.description: Free-text rationale surfaced in the approval UI and audit log. Never parsed or executed; purely informational for the human approver.
